prompt: Produce exactly one concise image caption (a single sentence, one line, preferably 15–35 words). Use only visually verifiable facts and avoid inference or speculation. For the caption include these visible elements (if present): 1) subject with brief appearance cues (approximate age if obvious, hair/clothing color or pattern), 2) explicit action or pose and a positional relation (foreground/background, left/right, on/at/in), 3) concrete objects/accessories with colors, materials, textures (e.g., metal, wood, diamond‑plate, hoses, case, amplifier), and 4) one scene or lighting cue and any notable occlusion or reflection. Mention numeric counts only when objects/people are clearly separable. Do not label professions, emotions, intentions, or use hedging words (probably, appears, seems, likely); prefer precise object labels over generic terms. Order words so the most discriminative tokens come first (object → color/material → pose → accessory → scene/occlusion). Output nothing but the single-sentence caption.
